extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, reissue applicants, and USPTO examiners handling reissue patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing, filing, and prosecuting a U.S. reissue patent application, including specification/drawing format, oaths/declarations, assignee consent, priority/benefit claims, and examiner processing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legible copy requirements (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: FR 1.98(a)(2) requires a legible copy of: (A) each foreign patent; (B) each publication or that portion which caused it to be listed, other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office; (C) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims, and any drawing of the application, or that portion of the application which caused it to be listed including any claims directed to that portion; and (D) all other information or that portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit legible copies of the exact portions that caused the reference to be listed; follow 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) when preparing an IDS or otherwise submitting references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose material information (37 CFR 1.56) and consequences of not providing copies
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue applicant has a continuing duty under 37 CFR 1.56 to timely apprise the Office of any information which is material to the patentability of the claims under consideration in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office imposes no responsibility on the reissue applicant to resubmit all references cited in the patent, but if a copy of a non-U.S. reference cited in the original patent is not available except from the reissue applicant and the applicant has not submitted it, the examiner will not consider that reference and will not list it on the PTO-892 form; examiners will line-through references listed on PTO/SB/08 for which no copy is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application must contain same parts as original (37 CFR 1.171)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reissue must contain the same parts required for an application for an original patent, complying with all the rules relating thereto except as otherwise provided, and in addition must comply with requirements relating to reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the formal requirements for patent applications (e.g., 37 CFR 1.52) unless specifically modified for reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents: entire specification, claims, drawings; no new matter; two-year limit for broadened claims (37 CFR 1.173)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reissue must contain the entire specification, including the claims, and the drawings of the patent. No new matter shall be introduced into the application. No reissue patent shall be granted enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years from the grant of the original patent, pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the reissue includes a full copy of the printed patent specification and drawings; do not add new matter; note the two-year bar for claim broadening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification copy format and required accompanying documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire specification, including the claims, of the patent for which reissue is requested must be furnished as a copy of the printed patent, in double column format, each page on only one side of a single sheet of paper. A re-typed specification is not acceptable. A copy of any disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321), certificate of correction (37 CFR 1.322–1.324), or reexamination certificate (37 CFR 1.570) issued in the patent must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve columnar structure and formatting rules (37 CFR 1.52); include prior certificates/disclaimers so the reissue is relative to the patent as last changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit a clean copy of each drawing sheet of the printed patent at the time the reissue application is filed. If such copy complies with 37 CFR 1.84, no further drawings will be required. Where a drawing of the reissue application is to include any changes relative to the patent being reissued, the changes to the drawing must be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.173(b)(3). The Office will not transfer the drawings from the patent file to the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clean drawing copies that comply with drawing rules; make any drawing changes in the manner prescribed by the reissue drawing rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment presentation and formatting rules (37 CFR 1.173(b)-(e),(g) and 1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment may be submitted at the time of filing of a reissue application either by (A) physically incorporating the changes within the specification by cutting the column of the printed patent and inserting the added material and rejoining the remainder of the column (markings pursuant to 37 CFR 1.173(d) must be used) with the columnar structure preserved and the physically modified page complying with 37 CFR 1.52(a)(1), or (B) providing a separate amendment paper with the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A caret and line from text to a newly added phrase typed legibly in the margin is deemed to satisfy the 'written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink' requirement under 1.52(a)(1)(iv). Presentation of insertions/deletions as part of original reissue specification is an amendment under 37 CFR 1.173(b); follow MPEP §1453 for amendment practice. A preliminary amendment cancelling all original claims without presenting any new claims is inappropriate under 37 CFR 1.115(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims requirement at filing (reissue vs 37 CFR 1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision allowing an application to be accorded a filing date 'with or without' claims (37 CFR 1.53(b)) does not apply in reissue applications because 37 CFR 1.173(a)(1) requires the entire specification, including the claims, of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file a reissue application without claims; a preliminary amendment that cancels all claims without new claims is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to submit a typed clean copy and petition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the changes to be made to the patent are so extensive that reading and understanding the specification is extremely difficult and error-prone, a clean, typed copy of the specification may be submitted if accompanied by a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 for waiver of 37 CFR 1.125(d) and 37 CFR 1.173(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and file a petition under 1.183 with necessary showing if requesting a typed copy in lieu of modified printed patent pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments relative to prior changes/certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.173(a)(1) and related rules, where there was a prior change to the patent (made via a certificate, reissue, disclaimer, etc.), the first amendment of the subject reissue application must be made relative to the patent as changed by the prior proceeding or mechanism for changing the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the reissue amendment references the current form of the patent including any earlier certificates or corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose related proceedings (37 CFR 1.178(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.178(b) requires reissue applicants to call to the attention of the Office any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved, such as interferences, reissues, reexaminations, or litigation, and the results of such proceedings; this duty is continuing from filing until abandonment or issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and provide papers from related proceedings (motions, pleadings, court decisions, orders) and keep the Office informed throughout prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original patent surrender not required
rubrics_metrics.description: It is no longer required that the reissue applicant physically surrender the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the original patent for surrender; follow MPEP §1416 for additional procedural notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority/benefit claim requirements and ADS (35 U.S.C. 119/120; 37 CFR 1.76, 1.55, 1.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, the reissue applicant must provide a claim for priority/benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119 or 120 in the reissue application. Benefit and priority claims made in the patent for which reissue is sought do not carry over into the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any reissue filed on or after September 16, 2012, priority/benefit claim information must be in an application data sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76 and must be made within the time periods set forth in 37 CFR 1.55 and 1.78 unless a petition for unintentionally delayed claim is filed. An ADS is required if an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is made by a person other than the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) may be filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, the reissue applicant may file an Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow IDS practice as applicable to reissue applications; include required copies and conform to 37 CFR 1.98 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing compliance for nucleotide/amino acid sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application that discloses nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences must comply with the sequence rules (37 CFR 1.831 - 1.839 for reissue applications filed on or after July 1, 2022 and 37 CFR 1.821 - 1.825 for reissue applications filed before July 1, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §2412 et seq. for submission of Sequence Listing XMLs and MPEP §2422.03 et seq. for submission of Sequence Listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing procedures and transmittal form (PTO/AIA/50) and EFS options
rubrics_metrics.description: For expedited processing, new and continuing reissue application filings under 37 CFR 1.53(b) may be addressed to Mail Stop REISSUE. Reissue applications may be filed through the USPTO patent electronic filing system (EFS); when filing electronically an applicant should choose the 'reissue' radio button. All new reissue filings should include a copy of a completed Reissue Patent Application Transmittal Form (PTO/AIA/50) to ensure recognition as a reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail Stop REISSUE should only be used for the initial filing; do not use it for subsequent correspondence. Include a copy of the completed PTO/AIA/50 with the initial filing; form reproduced in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of oath/declaration and fee submission (37 CFR 1.53(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration, any matters ancillary thereto (such as consent of assignee), and the basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee may be submitted after the filing date pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will accord a filing date and send a missing parts notice setting a period for filing missing parts and payment of any surcharges required under 37 CFR 1.53(f) and 1.16(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applicant identity and assignee consent requirements (37 CFR 1.172 and 3.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue applicant is the original patentee, or the current patent owner if there has been an assignment. A reissue application must be accompanied by the written consent of all assignees, if any, currently owning an undivided interest in the patent. All assignees consenting to the reissue must establish their ownership in the patent by filing in the reissue application a submission in accordance with 37 CFR 3.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no assignee exists, applicant should affirmatively state that fact (e.g., check 'NO' box on item 8 of Form PTO/AIA/50). Mere filing of small/micro entity assertions does not relieve the requirement to affirmatively state that no assignee exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration rules for reissue (37 CFR 1.175)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor, or each individual who is a joint inventor of a claimed invention in a reissue application must execute an oath or declaration for the reissue application, except as provided in 37 CFR 1.64. The inventor's oath or declaration may be signed by the assignee of the entire interest if: (1) the application does not seek to enlarge the scope of the claims of the original patent; or (2) the application for the original patent was filed under 37 CFR 1.46 by the assignee of the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue applicant may file a substitute statement in lieu of the inventor’s oath or declaration as provided in 37 CFR 1.64. For continuation/divisional reissue applications, a copy of an earlier reissue oath/declaration may be used provided certain conditions (no claim broadening or earlier original filing-by-assignee conditions) are met. See MPEP §1414 for forms PTO/AIA/05 and PTO/AIA/06 and additional content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding or deleting inventors in reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is to be added in a reissue application, a proper reissue oath or declaration including the signatures of all of the inventors is required. If one or more inventors are being deleted, an oath or declaration must be supplied over the signatures of the remaining inventors. A deleted inventor need not sign the oath or declaration, but if that inventor has any ownership interest in the patent, the signature of that inventor must be supplied in a consent to the filing of the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §1412.04 for correction of inventorship via reissue and ensure appropriate consents where ownership interests exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee consent signature rules and petition/waiver process
rubrics_metrics.description: The consent of assignee must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the consent may be signed by the assignee or a patent practitioner of record. For applications filed before September 16, 2012, the consent must be signed by the assignee. Where the assignee is a juristic entity, the consent may be signed by a person in the organization having apparent authority or by a person who makes a statement of authorization to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the written consent of all assignees cannot be obtained, applicant may petition the Office of Petitions for a waiver under 37 CFR 1.183 (petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f) required). A reissue application may be examined but will not be allowed or issued without the required assignee consents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of assignee consent copies in continuation/divisional reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a continuation reissue application is filed with a copy of the assignee consent from the parent reissue application, and the parent reissue application is not to be abandoned, the copy of the consent is generally not adequate for the continuation reissue application. If the parent reissue application is, or will be, abandoned, the copy should be accepted. Where a divisional reissue application is filed in response to a restriction requirement made in the parent reissue application, the assignee need not file a consent to the divided-out invention because consent has already been provided in the parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will accord a filing date and the examiner will require submission of a proper assignee consent unless the parent is abandoned or the divisional exception applies. Use form paragraph guidance (e.g., 14.15) to notify applicant of deficient consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of ownership under 37 CFR 3.73 when assignee consent is provided
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee that consents to the filing of the reissue application must also establish that it is the assignee/owner of the patent. Ownership must be established by either (A) filing in the reissue application documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee, or (B) specifying in the record of the reissue application where such evidence is recorded in the Office (e.g., reel and frame number). The submission must be accompanied by a statement affirming that the documentary evidence of the chain of title was, or concurrently is being, submitted for recordation pursuant to 37 CFR 3.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 3.73 statement is not accompanied by the required recordation statement, the 3.73 statement will not be accepted and the assignee will not have established right to take action; submit documentary evidence or reel/frame citation and confirm recordation concurrently when filing consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature authority for 37 CFR 3.73 ownership submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission with respect to 37 CFR 3.73 to establish ownership must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, a patent practitioner of record may sign the statement (see 37 CFR 3.73(d)(3)). For applications filed before September 16, 2012, the signature of an attorney or agent of record is not sufficient unless that attorney/agent is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 3.73 submission is not signed by an appropriate party, use form paragraphs (e.g., 14.16.01–14.16.04.fti) to notify applicant and instruct how to correct; a non-recognized officer may sign only if the record includes a duly signed empowerment statement (see form paragraph 14.16.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner inspection obligation on initial receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon initial receipt of a reissue application, the examiner should inspect the application to determine whether the submission under 37 CFR 1.172 and 37 CFR 3.73 establishing the ownership of the assignee is present and sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ownership/consent submissions are missing or insufficient, use the appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 14.16, 14.15) to object and request the necessary papers; follow MPEP instructions for prosecution or allowance sequencing where consent issues exist.
